chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that whatever erroneous judgement is made regarding blood (diyah) or cutting (amputation), it is upon the public treasury of the Muslims.

key_terms.بَيْتُ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.قَطْعٍ: Cutting (referring to amputation as a punishment)

ai.seo_question: Who bears the cost when judges make an error in criminal punishments?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of 'gharamat al-qudat' (judicial expenses), establishing that errors in criminal punishments like blood money or amputation are borne by the public treasury (bayt al-mal) rather than the litigants. This ruling, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the judgment of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), underscores the state's responsibility for judicial accuracy and protects citizens from financial loss due to clerical or procedural mistakes by the judiciary.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged that whatever erroneous judgement (is made) regarding blood, or cutting, so it is upon the public treasury of the Muslims’.
